correctness.rationale: The source gives unique endpoints and rank \(h=n+2\). For the proposed center, every coordinate boundary is at least \(r\) away, while a cover normal has norm \(\sqrt2\) and the longest-path level increases by at least one across every cover, giving distance at least \(r\). A longest min-to-max saturated chain gives the reverse inequality: the lower endpoint distance, \(h\) cover distances, and upper endpoint distance telescope to \(1\geho(2+h\sqrt2)\). Therefore the constructed ball is feasible and no larger ball can fit.

value.rationale: Generalized snake posets were introduced specifically as a rank-parametrized family whose order-polytope normalized volumes vary substantially with the snake word; the source identifies snake and ladder volume extremals at fixed rank. The new result shows a complementary rigidity phenomenon: the Euclidean inradius ignores all of that word-level combinatorics and depends only on rank. It also gives an explicit optimal center for every word. This is a natural exact metric invariant of the full family rather than a low-dimensional computation or arbitrary slice.
